subject: Leadership recap: quantifying ops risk & pilot gating for HealthSpan
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Claire Reynolds <claire@healthspan.com>, Alex Jones <alex.jones@healthspan.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Leadership recap: quantifying ops risk & pilot gating for HealthSpan

Claire / Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Below is a concise recap and proposed gating criteria for the pilot so your execs (and procurement) have a crisp view of what success looks like and what risks we need to mitigate before a production rollout.

Key pain points you confirmed:
- Bursty monthly inference spikes (billing variance + surprise overages).
- Unpredictable tail latency during peak ingestion windows impacting patient-facing workflows.
- Need for stronger auditability (retention, per-request audit logs) and VPC-specific connectivity for PHI compliance.

Stated goals for a 90-day pilot (aligned to business outcomes):
1) Latency: P50 < 120 ms, P95 < 400 ms for the primary inference flow (end-to-end).
2) Cost: measurable reduction in per-token inference cost vs current self-hosted baseline — target 30% unit cost improvement to justify continued rollout.
3) Reliability: <1 SLA-impacting outage (>=5m) for the pilot window; documented fallback to a cheaper model variant on capacity constraints.
4) Compliance: maintain customer-owned VPC peering and 90-day audit log retention with export capability.

Proposed pilot scope (what Redwood will deliver):
- Dedicated test pool sized for current average qps + 2x burst capacity for three 2-week load events.
- Prefill/recorded KV-caching to replicate your query distribution and provide realistic latency/cost numbers.
- Per-request tracing and an audit export with sample log schema.
- One production-like failover run to validate fallback behaviour and canary routing.

Gating criteria (must be met before we transition to a paid Dedicated contract):
- Measured P95 latency below 400 ms on a production-representative load test.
- End-to-end runbooks and an ops playbook accepted by HealthSpan SRE/CISO.
- Legal sign-off on the data residency and KMS integration (we will provide an HSM/KMS integration checklist).
- Procurement accepts SOW scope and pilot pricing terms (attached draft).

Open asks / next steps (I’ll own coordination):
- Claire: confirm the exec-sponsor availability for a short 30-min alignment call the week of Sep 7 (we recommend Tue/Wed morning PDT).
- Alex (CISO): can you share the contact for the person who will own the security checklist? Ideally we capture any hard-blockers (e.g., additional encryption certs) up front.
- Procurement: please confirm target decision date for pilot approval (we noted Sep 21 on the call).

Attachments: redwood-performance-metrics.xlsx (preliminary latency/cost model), SOW-draft-v2.pdf (pilot scope & pricing).

I’ll follow up with a one-page ROI snapshot requested during the call; Karthik will draft the gating checklist for your security review.

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Naomi / team — I drafted a short gating checklist and flagged the primary operational risks; excerpt below. I suggest we (Redwood) own the following mitigations pre-pilot:

Operational risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Burst-induced queueing causing P95 spikes.
  Mitigation: Configure automatic burst buffers and set soft-limits with immediate fallback to a lower-capacity model variant.
- Risk: Log retention/ingest costs balloon during debug windows.
  Mitigation: Provide sampling rules + compressed export to HealthSpan-owned S3; include ingestion caps in pilot SOW.
- Risk: Network egress failure between VPC peering and Redwood endpoints.
  Mitigation: Canary region failover plus a documented runbook; run two simulated DR tests during the pilot.

I attached "pilot-gate-checklist.xlsx" to Karthik's internal note (Naomi; if you want, I can incorporate into the SOW draft).

Karthik
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
